title: Reversed Squares: High Effort, Repeated Runtime Failures
description: Very high activity with multiple submissions, but no successful pass state.
why_interesting: Shows why sheer effort is not enough: repeated runs and submissions can still end in zero without targeted diagnosis.

timeline.text: Task: transform a list into reversed squared values. The session begins with runtime errors.
After dozens of attempts, runtime errors still dominate. Likely editing without isolating the first failing case.
Midway status is still similar: many attempts, little stability. A classic thrashing signature.
Late in the session, the same failure mode persists. They may be trying broad rewrites instead of minimal reproducible checks.
Some runs shift from runtime to wrong answer, but still no pass. Progress exists but is not consolidated.
First submission still has runtime failure (score 0).
Another submission also fails at runtime. This is a useful moment for discussing “stop-and-diagnose” interventions.
Session ends without recovery. Strong example for coaching protocols that reduce unproductive loops.
